<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard sources and build procedures for a 32-bit compatibility library (lib32-pam) on Arch Linux. During the execution of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, only the global scope, `pkgver()` function, and source fetching are evaluated.

The `source` array uses a git repository from the legitimate upstream (github.com/linux-pam/linux-pam) with a signed tag reference (`?signed#tag=${_tag}`), which is consistent with secure AUR packaging practices when combined with `validpgpkeys`. The PGP keys listed correspond to trusted maintainers of the Linux-PAM project. The `pkgver()` function performs a simple `git describe --tags` call within the checked-out repository, which is safe as it operates only on the already-fetched git history and does not trigger network operations or execute untrusted code. There are no command substitutions, remote executions, or data exfiltration attempts in the top-level scope or `pkgver()`.

No dangerous operations occur during sourcing: no `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or similar constructs appear in executable contexts outside of build functions (which are skipped). The use of `b2sums` with a valid hash and `options=(!emptydirs)` are benign packaging choices.
</details>
